scope: FIRST independent English SCI, fidelity, text readability and applicability of the unchanged approved shared fig-03 inventory. All six objects and ten final paragraphs reviewed. No image inspection.

scientificAssessment.signedHookeLaw: With the rightward axis and equilibrium origin, x>0 gives F_x<0 and x<0 gives F_x>0 for k>0. Magnitude proportionality is distinguished from signed force. The spring force is the net horizontal force only under the stated no-resistance approximation; weight and support cancel vertically.
scientificAssessment.inertiaAndReferenceFrame: The constant-mass Newton equation is explicitly restricted to an inertial reference frame and uses the net force. Inertia is not introduced as an additional force. When the net force is zero at a crossing, existing velocity can persist; no accelerating frame or fictitious-force interpretation is smuggled into the derivation.
scientificAssessment.accelerationVersusVelocity: At x=0 the retained equation gives a_x=0. It does not give v=0. For a nontrivial ideal spring oscillation the crossing speed is nonzero, whereas at a turning point velocity is zero with nonzero restoring acceleration. The English statement velocity need not be zero is valid and avoids the common confusion.
scientificAssessment.generalizationLimits: The English accurately translates the current Chinese condition-limited statement: a linear restoring force and negligible resistance permit the undriven harmonic-oscillator form; free oscillation alone does not. The original broad claim is not treated as proof. Real damping adds a velocity-dependent force and changes the equation.
scientificAssessment.independentJudgment: The existing Chinese delivery and native result are baselines, not historical SCI approval. Sign cases, division by positive nonzero mass, equilibrium acceleration, and model applicability were judged directly.
scientificAssessment.sourceExampleBoundary: The raw opening also mentions a ball on a string. The delivered Chinese deliberately focuses this lesson on the horizontal spring model; English follows that existing focus. No fresh English omission of a currently retained example is introduced.

blockFindings.finding: Faithfully retains the delivered Chinese introduction to the horizontal spring model: constant mass, Hooke-law spring, neglected friction and air resistance. These conditions legitimately bound the later equations and do not add a task.

Inertial reference frame correctly translates the Chinese qualification. The vector equation (1.1), mass/acceleration/net-force meanings, and warning against selecting one arbitrary force are unchanged and clear.

Rightward OX and equilibrium origin are retained. Weight/support balance justifies horizontal net force. Magnitudes are proportional while force and displacement have opposite signs; positive stiffness and the minus sign remain explicit. Equation (1.2) and Figure 3a/b/c references fit the approved spring-state inventory.
Substitution gives the unchanged ma_x=-kx and division by mass gives the unchanged a_x=-(k/m)x. Acceleration component, axis and equation labels (1.3)/(1.4) remain correctly identified.

Constant m and k imply constant k/m; greater displacement magnitude gives greater restoring acceleration magnitude. The English preserves the current Chinese clarification that zero acceleration at equilibrium does not imply zero velocity. It is not generalized to a pendulum's full acceleration.

The same-form claim is explicitly conditional on linear restoring action and negligible resistance, not on free oscillation alone. This accurately conveys the delivered Chinese limitation and is scientifically valid rather than an unconditional equivalence.

paragraphFindings.finding: Model assumptions precede the equations; short sentences preserve the spring-only delivered scope.
The inertial-frame/net-force statement and vector equation are correct; no force of inertia is asserted.
Axis, origin, vertical force balance and magnitude proportionality are unambiguous and fit Figure 3a.
Opposite signs and F_x=-kx fit stretched-right and compressed-left states, Figure 3b/c.
Positive k and the directional meaning of the minus sign are retained without treating k as negative.
The horizontal Newton equation and meaning of a_x are correct and token-identical.
Division by mass yields (1.4) without changing sign or coefficient.
Constant coefficient and displacement-dependent restoring acceleration are distinguished from constant acceleration.
Equilibrium crossing can have zero acceleration with nonzero velocity; inertia is consistent with Newton's law.
The final generalization is bounded; no claim that all free oscillations satisfy the equation remains.

figureApplicability.method: Read the existing approved source.inventory and review bindings as text; hash the current spec/SVG/render/review bytes once. No pixels, rerender or source-fidelity review.
inventoryFindings: Shared rightward X axis, O and equilibrium guide match the English coordinate convention.
State a is at equilibrium with no force arrow; the English references it for the origin, not for a nonzero force.
State b has a right-displaced ball, stretched spring and leftward F arrow, consistent with x>0 and F_x<0.
State c has a left-displaced ball, compressed spring and rightward F arrow, consistent with x<0 and F_x>0.
The maximum-displacement marker in b and displacement marker in c are not replaced by invented values; English changes neither label meaning nor figure identity.
The Latin a/b/c references agree with the already localized panel identities. The shared figure remains attached to object 2 after its final paragraph.

research.purpose: Scientific applicability of damping to the undriven equation; not translation research.
research.method: Official URL read as rendered text with cloak-fetch, no screenshots.

sources.title: University Physics Volume 1, 15.5 Damped Oscillations
sources.support: Damping modifies ma=-kx by adding a velocity-dependent resisting force; underdamped motion oscillates with decaying amplitude, and strong damping can prevent oscillation.
